The Chief Information Commissioner or any Information Commissioner can be removed by the President on grounds of proved misbehavior or incapacity after a Supreme Court inquiry.

items: Removal Authority: Remember that Commissioners are removed by the President, not by Parliament.
Prerequisite Inquiry: A Supreme Court inquiry is mandatory before removal on grounds of proved misbehavior or incapacity.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The President holds the authority to remove the Chief Information Commissioner and any Information Commissioner.
Removal must be based on grounds of proved misbehavior or incapacity.
A prior inquiry conducted by the Supreme Court is mandatory before any removal.
